text: 10 OVERDOSAGE Clinical Presentation Cardiovascular effects may include tachycardia and hypertension, but bradycardia and hypotension have also been reported. CNS manifestations include CNS depression, agitation, hallucinations, delusions, seizures, respiratory depression, and coma. Overdose can be fatal, especially in combination with CNS depressant drugs (including alcohol). Serotonin syndrome, leading to muscle rigidity, tremor, and hyperthermia, has been reported [see Warnings and Precautions (5.1) ]. Treatment of Overdose Monitor for CNS and respiratory depression, managing airway as needed. Gastrointestinal decontamination procedures should generally be avoided. Aspiration may result from CNS depression and seizures; emesis is not recommended. Extracorporeal elimination such as hemodialysis or plasmapheresis have no clinical benefit. Consider contacting the Poison Help line (1-800-222-1222) or a medical toxicologist for additional overdose management recommendations. Annual reports by the National Poison Data System (NPDS) from 2017-2021 contain 33,743 cumulative incidents of single drug exposures (ingestions) involving the most commonly prescribed skeletal muscle relaxants (SMRs). When grouped into distinct medical outcome categories by severity of resulting reaction or death, (i) metaxalone, and (ii) methocarbamol are reported at lower rates than other SMRs of “Moderate effect” or “Major effect or Death” 1 . 1 See https://doi.org/10.1080/15563650.2022.2132768 pg 1642 for Medical Outcome definitions.
